  1. DEFINITIONS

References to Schedules and Sections shall mean Schedules and Sections of this Agreement and, unless a contrary intention appears, references to persons shall include individuals, corporations, partnerships and unincorporated bodies of persons. When used in this Agreement, unless the contrary intention appears, the following words and expressions have the following meanings:

Accepting Parties has the meaning set out in Section 9.4.1.

Affiliate means, with respect to any person, any other person that, directly or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, either controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such person (as control is defined in the Finnish Accounting Act (Kirjanpitolaki 1336/1997, as amended)), provided, however, that the Company shall not for the purposes of this Agreement be considered an Affiliate of any Shareholder.

Agreement means this shareholders’ agreement and the Schedules hereto.

Articles of Association means the articles of association of the Company, as amended from time to time.

Bad Leaver has the meaning set out in Section 8.2.1.

Board means the board of directors of the Company.

Breaching Party has the meaning set out in Section 15.2.

Business means the business of the Company or the companies belonging to the same group, as carried out by the Company and such companies from time to time.

Called Shares has the meaning set out in Section 9.4.2.

Common Share has the meaning set out in Section 5.1.

Companies Act means the Finnish Limited Liability Companies Act (osakeyhtiölaki, 624/2006, as amended).

Company has the meaning set out in Section 1.

Confidential Information means:

  1. the terms and other contents of this Agreement;
  2. any and all non-public information of any kind and in any form, including, without limitation, all technical, financial and commercial information, know-how, client lists and other proprietary business information regarding the Company and/or its Business;
  3. any and all non-public information of any kind and in any form relating to a Shareholder or its Affiliates; and
  4. any other information that is identified as confidential by the disclosing Party at the time it is disclosed.

Discloser has the meaning set out in Section 11.1.

Drag-Along Notice has the meaning set out in Section 9.4.2.

Drag-Along Option has the meaning set out in Section 9.4.1.

Early Leaver has the meaning set out in Section 8.2.2.

Effective Date means the date of this Agreement.

Employment Contracts Act means the Finnish Employment Contracts Act (työsopimuslaki 55/2001, as amended).

Equity Securities means special rights referred to in Section 1 of Chapter 10 of the Companies Act, option rights (in Finnish: “optio-oikeus”), convertible loans, subscription rights or any other securities or instruments issued by the Company from time to time which can be converted into Shares or carry or have attached thereto a right to subscribe for Shares (excluding, however, any contractual rights based on this Agreement).

[ESOP has the meaning set out in Section 5.4.1.]

Exempted Issuance means issuances of Shares:

  1. to employees, consultants and advisors of the Company or to independent industry expert members of the Board (i) under the ESOP, or (ii) under any other equity-based incentive scheme;
  2. in connection with corporate or business acquisitions for the purposes of the payment of the purchase price, in each case subject to Section 7.2; or
  3. in connection with share splits carried out at the same ratio with respect to all Share classes.

Fair Market Value means the value of the Shares to be purchased as agreed by and between the relevant Parties and in the event such agreement is not reached within thirty (30) days, the value of such Shares calculated based on the valuation of the Company in an equity financing round completed within the preceding six (6) months, or, in the absence of such a financing round, the value of the Shares determined by an independent and reputable investment bank or expert specialised in company and business valuations appointed by the relevant Parties or the Board acting in good faith at the request of any relevant Party. The cost of the valuation shall be borne equally by the Company and the relevant Party or Parties, unless the request for valuation has been clearly unreasonable in which event the Party requesting the valuation shall bear the costs.

Founders has the meaning set out in Section 1.

Good Leaver has the meaning set out in Section 8.2.3.

Holding Company means a legal entity through which a Shareholder holds Shares.

Intellectual Property Rights means copyrights (excluding paternity rights), copyright related rights, know-how, trademarks, domain-names, utility models, logos and trade names, product descriptions, patents, innovations, discoveries, trade secrets, ideas, methods, rights in designs, computer software, and scientific, technical and product information relating to the Company (and any of its Affiliate) or arising from the Business of the Company (and any of its Affiliates), regardless of whether registered or not and including application for grant of any of the foregoing and all rights or forms of protection having equivalent or similar effect to any of the foregoing, which may subsist now or at any time hereafter, anywhere in the world.

Investment Agreement has the meaning set out in Section 3.3.

Investors has the meaning set out in Section 1.

Liquidation Event means (i) a Trade Sale or (ii) liquidation, dissolution, winding up or bankruptcy of the Company.

Material Breach has the meaning set out in Section 15.1.

Party has the meaning set out in Section 1.

Personal Data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person (‘data subject’) as defined in Article 4(1)1 in the General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 (GDPR).

Purchaser(s) has the meaning set out in Section 9.5.1.

Qualified Majority means the Shareholders holding at least two thirds (2/3) of the Shares held by all Shareholders and including always the Shareholders holding more than fifty per cent (50%) of the Series Seed Shares.

Representatives has the meaning set out in Section 11.1.

Selling Shareholder has the meaning set out in Section 9.5.1.

Selling Shareholder’s Notice has the meaning set out in Section 9.5.2.

Series Seed Share has the meaning set out in Section 5.1.

Share means any class of shares (including the Common Shares and the Series Seed Shares) and Equity Securities in the Company.

Shareholder has the meaning set out in Section 1.

Shareholders with Purchase Right has the meaning set out in Section 8.1.2.

Shareholders’ Meeting means the ordinary or extraordinary shareholders’ meeting of the Company.

Subsidiary means each legal entity directly or indirectly owned or controlled by the Company (as control is defined in Section 5 of Chapter 1 of the Accounting Act (Kirjanpitolaki 1336/1997, as amended) for so long as such control lasts.

Third-Party Purchaser has the meaning set out in Section 9.4.1.

Trade Sale means any of the following events: (i) a sale to a third party of more than [two thirds (2/3)] of the Shares; (ii) sale to an existing Shareholder of all or substantially all of the Shares not already held by such Shareholder; (iii) sale, transfer, exclusive license or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company; or (iv) merger, reorganisation or consolidation or other transaction subsequent to which the Shareholders will, as a result of such transaction, possess less than [two thirds (2/3)] of the shares of the surviving or new entity.

Trade Sale Offer has the meaning set out in Section 9.4.1.

Transfer means, with respect to any class of Shares or any interest therein, (i) to offer, sell, grant any pledge, option, right or warrant to purchase or purchase, any option or lend or otherwise transfer (including but not limited to by way of the liquidation of community property between spouses, or transfer to a spouse or to an ascendant or a descendant) or dispose of, directly or indirectly, any such Shares or interests therein; or (ii) enter into any swap or other arrangement that transfers to any third party, in whole or in part, any of the economic rights of any Shares or interests therein, whether any such transaction described in clause (i) or (ii) above is to be settled in cash, by delivery of any shares or interests in any other legal entity or otherwise. When used as a noun, the term Transfer shall have the correlative meaning.

Transfer Notice has the meaning set out in Section 9.2.1.

Transferring Shareholder has the meaning set out in Section 9.2.1.

Working Shareholders has the meaning set out in Section 1.

  1. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE

Upon entering into this Agreement, the Parties agree on certain rights and obligations of the Shareholders and the Company, as well as on the management of the Company.

On the Effective Date, the Company is [and its Subsidiaries are] engaged in the business of [specify scope of business] (the Business).

On the even date herewith, the Parties have executed an investment agreement relating to the Company (the Investment Agreement).

The objective of the Parties is to manage and develop the Business and the operations of the Company in order to maximise the value of the Shares. The Parties also intend to raise additional funds for the Company. The Parties acknowledge and understand that a new investor who will provide such funds might require the Shareholders to enter into a new shareholders’ agreement and that the new investor may require that the shares issued to it shall be preferred shares.

The Parties may also enter into a minority shareholders’ agreement to which certain minority shareholders and/or transferees of Shares are required to adhere as decided by the Board. In the event of any discrepancy between this Agreement and the possible minority shareholders’ agreement, this Agreement shall prevail.

The Shareholders warrant that they have carefully and independently evaluated the rights and obligations arising out of this Agreement, as well as the risks and opportunities associated with it.

  1. GENERAL OBLIGATIONS

The Working Shareholders agree to contribute to the Company’s success and to enable it to achieve the objectives set forth in the business plan of the Company (as amended from time to time by the Board).

Each Shareholder undertakes, also through the members of the Board or other representatives appointed by it, at the Shareholders’ Meetings, at the meetings of the Board and on any other occasion to exercise its voting rights and to act otherwise in a way necessary to ensure the proper realization of and compliance with the terms of this Agreement and the Articles of Association. For the avoidance of doubt, the above does not mean that the Shareholder is required at all times to be present or represented in the Shareholders’ Meeting or at the meetings of the Board.

  1. CAPITALISATION AND SHARES
    1. Common and Preferred Shares

The Company has two (2) separate classes of shares: common shares (the Common Shares) and preferred series seed shares (the Series Seed Shares). The Series Seed Shares shall have preference as set out in Section 5.2 over the Common Shares in the Liquidation Events and shall be convertible into Common Shares at any time as set out in Section 5.3 below but otherwise the Common Shares and the Series Seed Shares shall have equal rights in the Company. Each Common Share and Series Seed Share shall carry one (1) vote in a Shareholders’ Meeting.

    1. Liquidation Preference

In the event of any Liquidation Event of the Company, the proceeds shall be paid to the Shareholders as follows:

  1. First, the greater of:
  2. the original subscription price paid for each Series Seed Share added with declared but unpaid dividends on each Series Seed Share; or
  3. the amount that the holder of Series Seed Shares would have received, had the Series Seed Shares been converted into Common Shares immediately prior to the Liquidation Event

shall be paid to the holders of the Series Seed Shares.

  1. Secondly, the remaining proceeds shall be distributed to the holders of Common Shares on a pro rata basis.
    1. Conversion

Each Series Seed Share shall be convertible into one (1) Common Share at any time upon the request of each holder of the Series Seed Shares, subject to adjustments for stock splits, reverse splits and the like.

    1. [Employee Stock Option Plan]

The Parties agree that stock options may be offered to the current or future key personnel of the Company (including outside expert members of the Board). For this purpose, the Company’s existing Shareholders have, on the date of this Agreement, made a resolution on the creation of the employee stock option plan (the ESOP) consisting of [10.0]% of all Shares (on a fully diluted basis) after the Closing (as defined in the Investment Agreement). The stock options issued under the ESOP shall entitle the holders to new Common Shares. The Investors and the Founders shall, subject to the prior written consent of the holders of the majority of the Series Seed Shares, agree on the structuring and other details of the ESOP.

The issuance of stock options or Shares pursuant to the ESOP shall always require the holder of stock options or Shares to adhere to this Agreement and/or to the possible minority shareholders’ agreement regarding the Company or an option agreement in accordance with Section 9.3.]

    1. Share Certificates; Minority Dividend

The Company has not issued any share certificates representing the Shares. The Shareholders hereby waive their right under the Companies Act to require the Board to issue share certificates, interim certificates, option certificates or similar certificates.

Each Shareholder waives its right to demand distribution of dividends pursuant to Section 7 of Chapter 13 of the Companies Act.

  1. FUTURE FINANCING
    1. General

The Parties acknowledge and accept that the Company may from time to time issue new Shares strictly in accordance with this Agreement.

It is expressly agreed and understood that the Shareholders shall not, under this Agreement or otherwise, unless expressly otherwise agreed in writing on a case-by-case basis, be obligated to participate in any possible issue of Shares or grant a loan to the Company or any Subsidiary, if applicable, or to guarantee or provide any security for any debt or other liability of the Company or any Subsidiary.

All Investors shall have a pro rata right, but not an obligation, to participate in subsequent issuances of any Shares on the same terms and conditions as any other Shareholder or third-party investor or financer, provided that the pre-emptive right of the Investors shall not apply to any Exempted Issuance. In addition, should any Investor choose not to purchase or subscribe to its full pro rata portion (calculated based on the Investor’s then-current shareholding) in such issuances of any Shares, the other Investors shall have the right to purchase or subscribe to the remaining pro rata portion of the Shares. In the event an Investor has not replied or notified the Company in writing of its participation in the issuance of the Shares within fourteen (14) days after having received a notice by letter or email from the Company about the terms of the issuance, it shall be deemed to have irrevocably waived its subscription right to its pro rata part of issued Shares.

    1. Third-Party Financing

In the event that the Company is raising funds (such as through a third-party financer as mentioned under Section 6.1), the Shareholders understand that there may be a need to enter into a new shareholders’ agreement or other agreements (such as an investment agreement or a subscription agreement) regarding the Company and/or to amend the Articles of Association as well as to take other actions to secure the Company’s financing. Further, the Shareholders acknowledge that the Shares issued in such a financing round may be preferred shares with superior rights over the current Shares. Therefore, the Shareholders commit to vote in favour of any decisions in the Shareholders’ Meetings relating to amending the Articles of Association, directed Share issuances, other corporate resolutions on financing and any other matters required to complete the fund-raising, provided that the holders of more than 2/3 of the Series Seed Shares and the holders of more than 2/3 of the Common Shares vote for it. The Shareholders shall also sign and execute any shareholders’ agreement and other agreements (such as investment agreement or subscription agreement) required for completion of the above actions. If a Shareholder does not execute such agreement(s) or vote in favour of the above actions simultaneously with the other Shareholders, such Shareholder shall be deemed to have appointed the Board, or any person appointed by the Board, for that purpose to be its sole agent and attorney to execute all necessary agreements, to vote in favour of any matters and to take any other necessary actions on its behalf provided that if such agreements would impose any onerous obligations on a Shareholder adversely deviating from the obligations of other similarly situated Shareholders, the consent of the affected Shareholder to such agreement shall be specifically required.

  1. GOVERNANCE OF THE COMPANY

The Board shall consist of a maximum of five (5) members, of which two (2) members and their personal deputy members shall be elected by holders of the majority of the Common Shares and one (1) member elected by holders of the majority of the Series Seed Shares. Other members of the Board, if any, shall be appointed by the Shareholders in accordance with the Companies Act.

In addition to any other approval required under the Companies Act and the Articles of Association, the Company shall not, and the Shareholders shall procure that the Company will not, without the written consent of the holders of the majority of the Series Seed Shares (and irrespective of whether such decision shall be made at the Shareholders’ Meeting, at the meeting of the Board or otherwise):

  1. adversely change the rights of the Series Seed Shares or amend the Articles of Association;
  2. issue, redeem, purchase or otherwise acquire, or sell or otherwise transfer any Shares [other than in connection with the ESOP or pursuant to a Compensatory Issue (as defined in the Investment Agreement)];
  3. declare or pay any dividend or make a decision on any other asset distribution;
  4. change the number of the Board members;
  5. merge, demerge, liquidate or dissolve the Company, including any Liquidation Event;
  6. transfer, lease, license (other than licenses granted in the ordinary course of business on a non-exclusive basis), pledge or encumber assets or rights material to the Company’s Business;
  7. enter into any agreement or assignment with a Shareholder or its immediate family member or any entity controlled by a Shareholder and/or its immediate family member or make any amendments thereto; or
  8. hire or fire any Working Shareholders or amend the terms of service or employment agreements of the Working Shareholders.

Any and all matters referred to in this Section 7 concerning an Affiliate (including a Subsidiary, joint venture or branch) of the Company shall require the same majority as set out above in this Section 7.

The chairperson of the Board shall be elected by the Board from among the Board members. [At the next meeting of the Board on or after the Effective Date, [●] shall be elected to act as the chairperson of the Board.]

  1. Purchase OF SHARES FROM WORKING SHAREHOLDERS
    1. Working Commitment and Vesting

The Working Shareholders shall, subject to the permitted secondary occupations listed in the Schedule 2, use 100% of their business hours for the benefit of the Company or its Subsidiaries. The Common Shares owned by the Working Shareholders are subject to the purchase rights in accordance with the provisions of this Section 8.

If a Working Shareholder’s service or employment agreement is terminated, the Company primarily and the other Shareholders (other than the Working Shareholder whose service or employment agreement has been terminated) (the Shareholders with Purchase Right) secondarily on a pro rata basis to their then-current ownership of the Shares on a fully-diluted basis, have a right to purchase all or part of the Shares of such Working Shareholder against a cash payment as set forth in this Section 8.

The Common Shares of the Working Shareholders (including, for the sake of clarity, the Founders) shall vest as follows: 25% of the Common Shares shall vest one (1) year following the vesting commencement date with the remaining 75% of the Common Shares vesting in equal monthly instalments over the next three (3) years, thus one hundred percent (100%) of the Working Shareholder’s Common Shares will vest in four (4) years from the vesting commencement date.

The vesting commencement date shall mean (i) in respect of the Founders, the Effective Date, and (ii) in respect of the other Working Shareholders, the date of such Working Shareholder’s adherence to this Agreement. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary above, the Board shall have the right to agree on deviations to the above regular vesting periods on a case-by-case basis in writing, subject to the written consent of the Board member(s) appointed by the holders of the Series Seed Shares or, if such Board member has not been appointed, subject to the written consent of the holders of the majority of the Series Seed Shares.

In the case of employee stock options, the terms of the stock option scheme shall prevail, i.e. the Shares subscribed for with stock options shall not be subject to the vesting and purchase right provisions of this Section 8.

A Trade Sale shall accelerate the vesting of the Working Shareholder’s unvested Shares to the effect that all the Working Shareholder’s unvested Shares will vest upon the occurrence of a Trade Sale provided that, as a result of such Trade Sale, the respective Working Shareholder’s service or employment relationship is terminated.

    1. Bad Leaver, Early Leaver and Good Leaver

Irrespective of whether the Employment Contracts Act applies to the employment or service agreement of a Working Shareholder with the Company, if the employment or service relationship of a Working Shareholder terminates for any reason under circumstances where an employer would be entitled to:

  1. cancel an employment relationship pursuant to Section 1 of Chapter 8 of the Employment Contracts Act; or
  2. terminate the employment relationship pursuant to Section 2 of Chapter 7 of the Employment Contracts Act, excluding termination due to the death or permanent incapacity to work due to illness or injury;

such Working Shareholder shall be regarded as a Bad Leaver.

If the employment or service relationship of a Working Shareholder is cancelled or terminated by the respective Working Shareholder on his/her/their own initiative without a reason permitting cancellation or termination for reasons attributable to the employer pursuant to Section 1 of Chapter 8 of the Employment Contracts Act, such Working Shareholder shall be regarded as an Early Leaver. For the avoidance of doubt, if at the time of the Working Shareholder's resignation or termination on his/her/their own initiative, circumstances exist or existed that would have entitled the Company to cancel or terminate the Working Shareholder's employment or service relationship on grounds set out in Section 8.2.1, such Working Shareholder shall be regarded as a Bad Leaver notwithstanding the fact that the Working Shareholder resigned or terminated the relationship on his/her/their own initiative.

If the employment or service relationship of a Working Shareholder with the Company terminates for any other reason than the Bad Leaver reasons stated above in Section 8.2.1 or the Early Leaver reasons stated in Section 8.2.2, the respective Working Shareholder shall be regarded as a Good Leaver.

    1. Purchase of Shares

With respect to a Bad Leaver, all Common Shares may be purchased. The price for the Bad Leaver's unvested Common Shares to be purchased shall be the lower of (i) the original purchase price and/or subscription price of such Common Shares paid by the respective Working Shareholder; or (ii) 25% of the Fair Market Value of such Common Shares. The price for the Bad Leaver's vested Common Shares to be purchased shall be the higher of (i) the original purchase price and/or subscription price of such Common Shares paid by the respective Working Shareholder; or (ii) 25% of the Fair Market Value of such Common Shares.

With respect to an Early Leaver, all Common Shares may be purchased. The price for the Early Leaver's unvested Common Shares to be purchased shall be the lower of (i) the original purchase price and/or subscription price of such Common Shares paid by the respective Working Shareholder; or (ii) the Fair Market Value of such Common Shares. The price for the Early Leaver's vested Common Shares to be purchased shall be the higher of (i) the original purchase price and/or subscription price of such Common Shares paid by the respective Working Shareholder; or (ii) the Fair Market Value of such Common Shares.

With respect to a Good Leaver, only unvested Common Shares may be purchased. The price for the Good Leaver’s unvested Common Shares to be purchased shall be the higher of (i) the original purchase price and/or subscription price of such Common Shares paid by the respective Working Shareholder; or (ii) the Fair Market Value of such Common Shares. Any vested Common Shares of the Good Leaver that are not purchased pursuant to this Section 8.3.3 may be sold by the Good Leaver to any Shareholder, provided that the right of first refusal provisions set out in this Agreement shall apply to any such sale.

The termination of the Working Shareholder’s employment or service relationship with the Company shall be deemed to constitute an offer from such Working Shareholder primarily to the Company and secondarily to the Shareholders with Purchase Right to purchase all or part of the Working Shareholder’s applicable Common Shares. The notice regarding the exercise of the right to purchase the Working Shareholder’s applicable Common Shares under this Section 8 shall be given by the Company to all Shareholders with Purchase Right within two (2) months from the final day of the Working Shareholder’s employment or service agreement. If the Company has not confirmed within the above two (2) month period that it will purchase all the respective Working Shareholder’s applicable Common Shares, then the Shareholders with Purchase Right shall have, on a pro rata basis, the right to purchase all or part of the remaining part of the Working Shareholder’s applicable Common Shares by giving a written notice to all Shareholders with Purchase Right within four (4) months from the effective termination date of the Working Shareholder’s employment or service agreement. In the event one or more Shareholders with Purchase Right do not wish to exercise such right, the Shareholders with Purchase Right exercising the purchase right shall be entitled to purchase all Shares on a pro rata basis.

If the Company or the Shareholders with Purchase Right have not required the respective Working Shareholder’s applicable Common Shares to be purchased, the respective Working Shareholder shall have the right to keep such Common Shares.

The transfer of the Working Shareholder’s Common Shares to be purchased shall take place no later than within fourteen (14) days from the date of the above notice of the exercise of the purchase right in accordance with the Share Transfer Agreement substantially in a form attached hereto as Schedule 1 or as otherwise approved by the Board. In the event the Working Shareholder will not sign the Share Transfer Agreement, the acquisition and transfer of title of the Common Shares shall be deemed to have taken place upon the Company and/or the Shareholder(s) with Purchase Right exercising its purchase right notifying the respective Working Shareholder of its confirmation to acquire such Working Shareholder’s Common Shares or part of them and paying the corresponding purchase price to the bank account of the Working Shareholder used for the regular salary payments, or if the Working Shareholder has not provided details of such bank account, to a new bank account opened in the name of the Company specifically for the purposes of depositing the purchase price for the benefit of the Working Shareholder.

Each Party undertakes to perform such corporate and other actions as may be necessary for the full effectiveness of the provisions set out in this Section 8. The Parties acknowledge that any purchases of Shares in accordance with this Section 8 do not constitute a directed redemption of shares by the Company under the Companies Act, but rather a directed acquisition. In the event that any purchase of Shares under this Section 8 is considered, contrary to the Parties’ view, to be a directed redemption of Shares by the Company under the Companies Act, the Shareholders, by signing this Agreement, give their explicit and irrevocable consent to the directed redemption of the Shares they own directly or through their Holding Company, as well as the Shares owned by the other Shareholders according to the terms of this Section 8.

    1. Illustrative summary of Purchase Rights

The following table is included for illustrative purposes only and is intended to provide a summary of the purchase rights set out in this Section 8. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between this table and the provisions of Sections 8.1 to 8.3 above, the provisions of Sections 8.1 to 8.3 shall prevail.

Bad Leaver (Section 8.2.1) Early Leaver (Section 8.2.2) Good Leaver (Section 8.2.3)

Shares subject to purchase All Common Shares (vested and unvested) All Common Shares (vested and unvested) Unvested Common Shares only

Price – Unvested Shares Lower of (i) original purchase/subscription price; or (ii) 25% of Fair Market Value Lower of (i) original purchase/subscription price; or (ii) Fair Market Value Higher of (i) original purchase/subscription price; or (ii) Fair Market Value

Price – Vested Shares Higher of (i) original purchase/subscription price; or (ii) 25% of Fair Market Value Higher of (i) original purchase/subscription price; or (ii) Fair Market Value N/A – vested Common Shares are not subject to purchase rights

Retained Shares None – all Common Shares may be purchased None – all Common Shares may be purchased Vested Common Shares are retained; such shares may be sold to any Shareholder, subject to the right of first refusal provisions

  1. TRANSFER OF SHARES
    1. Limitations on Transfer

Before a Liquidation Event of the Company, no Shareholder shall, directly or indirectly, Transfer any of its Shares or any rights or interests therein, unless such Transfer is expressly allowed under the terms, conditions and provisions of this Agreement.

Unless otherwise expressly agreed in this Agreement, no transferee of the Shares, including, but not limited to any new person or entity subscribing for the Shares in the Company, shall become a shareholder of the Company, and no Shares shall be transferred on the books and records of the Company, until the transferee executes a written adherence agreement to this Agreement and/or to a minority shareholders’ agreement or an option agreement, as the case may be, in the form and substance satisfactory to the Board (including the vote of the member appointed by the holders of the Series Seed Shares), under which the transferee assumes all or part of the obligations of the transferor under this Agreement and agrees to be bound by and subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Agreement and/or the minority shareholders’ agreement or an option agreement, as the case may be, including any amendments made thereto. The Shareholders hereby irrevocably agree that such adherence agreement to this Agreement and/or to the minority shareholders’ agreement or an option agreement, as the case may be, when executed by the transferee and the Company (in a form approved by the Board as specified above) shall be valid and binding upon all the Parties. Each Party acknowledges and agrees that the restrictions on Transfers of Shares set forth in this Agreement are reasonable, given the purpose of this Agreement and the intent of the Parties to reach a common exit for the Company.

Notwithstanding anything else stated in this Agreement or the Articles of Association, each of the Investors may freely Transfer the Shares held by it to any fund(s) or companies owned or controlled by the Investor, any parent company (up and including the ultimate parent company) or other Affiliate of the Investor, or any general or limited partner or shareholder of the Investor, provided that, prior to such Transfer, the respective transferee shall have agreed in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement applicable to that Investor. If a transferee to whom Shares have been transferred pursuant to this paragraph ceases to be a company controlling the Investor, controlled by the Investor or under the same control as the Investor, such transferee is required to retransfer the Shares to the Investor. It is acknowledged and understood that the right of first refusal under Section 9.2 and the tag-along right under Section 9.5 shall not apply to any Transfer made pursuant to this paragraph.

Notwithstanding anything else stated in this Agreement or the Articles of Association, each of the Shareholders shall be entitled to Transfer the Shares held by it to a Holding Company provided that, prior to such Transfer, the respective Holding Company shall have agreed in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement applicable to that Shareholder. All the rights and obligations set out in this Agreement to a Shareholder apply also mutatis mutandis to a Holding Company through which such Shareholder holds Shares. The use of Holding Company does not in any way relieve the respective Shareholder from obligations under this Agreement, as the obligations of a Holding Company are parallel to those of the Shareholder utilising a Holding Company. A breach of this Agreement by a Holding Company is deemed as a breach by the Shareholder using it and vice versa. All Transfer restrictions and other obligations regarding Shares (including e.g. pledging and issuance and custody of share certificates) apply mutatis mutandis also to the shares in a Holding Company. If a Holding Company to whom Shares have been transferred pursuant to this paragraph shall cease to be a company wholly-owned or controlled by the Shareholder, such Holding Company shall be bound to retransfer the Shares to the respective Shareholder. It is acknowledged and understood that the right of first refusal under Section 9.2, the tag-along right under Section 9.5 and the right of redemption under the Articles of Association shall not apply to any Transfer made pursuant to this paragraph 9.1.4. Further, each Shareholder using a Holding Company undertakes that the respective Holding Company shall not, without the prior written consent of the holders of the majority of the Series Seed Shares:

  1. engage in any other activities (business or otherwise) than holding the Shares;
  2. in addition to the respective Shareholder, have any other holders of shares or any instruments that can be converted into or give a right to subscribe for or purchase shares in the Holding Company;
  3. have any other holdings or assets; or
  4. incur any debt or other liabilities or obligations.

The Parties irrevocably waive their right to redeem Shares under the redemption clause of the Articles of Association when the Transfer of the Shares is made in accordance with this Section 9.

[Notwithstanding anything else stated in this Agreement or the Articles of Association, any issuance of Series Seed Shares pursuant to a Compensatory Issue or any Transfer of Common Shares (and conversion thereof into Series Seed Shares) pursuant to a Compensatory Sale, in each case as defined in and carried out in accordance with the Investment Agreement, shall be permitted and shall not be subject to the right of first refusal under Section 9.2, the tag-along right under Section 9.5 or the right of redemption under the Articles of Association. Each Party undertakes to execute, make and do all such resolutions, documents and acts as may be necessary to effectively complete a Compensatory Issue and a Compensatory Sale in accordance with the Investment Agreement.]

    1. Right of First Refusal

Before a Shareholder Transfers a part or all of its Shares (the Transferring Shareholder), the Shares shall be offered first for redemption by the Company and secondly to the Shareholders on a pro rata basis according to the Shareholders’ then-current shareholdings by providing a written notice to the Company and the other Shareholders (the Transfer Notice). The Transfer Notice shall include at least the following information: the number of the Shares being sold, the transferee, the purchase price, the payment terms, the date of transfer of the title and all other material terms of the Transfer. The Transfer Notice shall constitute an irrevocable offer by such Transferring Shareholder to Transfer all Shares specified in the Transfer Notice in accordance with its terms.

If the Company wishes to use its right of first refusal partially or in full, it must make a binding offer to the Transferring Shareholder and notify the other Shareholders of the exercise of the right of first refusal in writing within thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of the Transfer Notice.

If the Company does not use its right of first refusal or does not use it with respect to all of the Shares, the other Shareholders shall have the secondary right of first refusal (without obligation) to purchase the Transferring Shareholder’s remaining Shares in accordance with the terms specified in the Transfer Notice, by giving a written notice to the Transferring Shareholder and all other Shareholders within fourteen (14) days from the end of the above thirty (30) day period. If more than one (1) Shareholder wishes to use his/her/their/its right of first refusal, the Shares shall be divided between such Shareholders in proportion to their then-current aggregate shareholdings in the Company, unless otherwise agreed between such acquiring Shareholders.

For the avoidance of doubt, if (and only when it is obvious that) the Company and the other Shareholders do not use their right of first refusal, as set above, in full, the Transferring Shareholder has the right to Transfer his/her/their/its Shares (or the part of them that have not been acquired under this Section 9.2) to the third party specified in the Transfer Notice at a price not less than the price specified in the Transfer Notice and otherwise on substantially similar terms to those specified in the Transfer Notice. This right of the Transferring Shareholder to Transfer his/her/their/its Shares shall be valid for ninety (90) days from the lapse of the above-mentioned fourteen (14) day period given to the other Shareholders to exercise their right of first refusal. After the above ninety (90) day period, the Transferring Shareholder shall not have the right to Transfer his/her/their/its Shares without recommencing the procedure under this Section 9.2.

For the avoidance of doubt, if a Shareholder does not exercise its right of first refusal, it shall be entitled to exercise the tag-along right under Section 9.5 in any subsequent Transfer of Shares.

    1. Adherence Agreement

All Transfers and new issuances of the Shares shall always be conditional upon the transferee committing to adhere to this Agreement (as a Shareholder and, when applicable, as an Investor or as a Working Shareholder) and/or to the possible minority shareholders’ agreement regarding the Company or an option agreement, in accordance with the decision of the Board (subject to the consent of the Board member(s) appointed by the holders of the Series Seed Shares) by signing a separate adherence agreement. The adherence agreement approved by the Board and executed by the Company shall be binding on all Parties. For the avoidance of doubt, no separate consent shall be required from any Party due to the adherence of a third party to this Agreement and/or the possible minority shareholders’ agreement or an option agreement, if the terms and conditions of this Agreement are complied with. The Board also has the right, subject to the consent of the member(s) of the Board appointed by the holders of the Series Seed Shares or, if such Board members have not been appointed, subject to the written consent of the holders of the majority of the Series Seed Shares, to agree with the third party on exceptions to the non-competition undertaking of this Agreement and/or the possible minority shareholders’ agreement.

    1. Drag-Along

If a bona fide arm’s length third party (the Third-Party Purchaser) makes a written offer on a Trade Sale (the Trade Sale Offer) at any time and the Qualified Majority wishes to accept such offer, such Shareholders (the Accepting Parties) shall have the option to require (the Drag-Along Option) that each Shareholder Transfers all his/her/their/its Shares to such Third-Party Purchaser (or as the Third-Party Purchaser shall direct in accordance with the provisions of this Section 9.4 (Drag-Along)) against the consideration for a Share determined by the Trade Sale Offer (or, if the Third-Party Purchaser wishes to execute the Trade Sale in any other way than by purchase of Shares, the Accepting Parties shall have the right to require that the Company and all Shareholders shall cause such Trade Sale to be executed) in accordance with the provisions of this Section 9.4 (Drag-Along).

The Accepting Parties may exercise the Drag-Along Option by giving written notice to that effect (a Drag-Along Notice) at any time before the Transfer of their Shares to the Third-Party Purchaser. A Drag-Along Notice shall specify that the other Shareholders are required to Transfer all their Shares (the Called Shares) pursuant to this Section 9.4 (Drag-Along), the Third-Party Purchaser (or its nominee) to whom they are to be transferred, the consideration for which the Called Shares are to be Transferred (calculated in accordance with this Section 9.4 (Drag-Along)), the proposed date of Transfer and other material terms of the transaction. Drag-Along Notice shall be irrevocable (unless waived in writing by the Accepting Parties) but will lapse if for any reason there is not a sale of the Accepting Parties’ Shares to the Third-Party Purchaser within sixty (60) days after the date of service of the Drag-Along Notice.

Completion of the sale of the Called Shares shall take place on the same date as the date proposed for completion of the sale of the Accepting Parties’ Shares unless all of the Shareholders agree otherwise.

If any Shareholder does not on completion of the sale of Called Shares execute transfers in respect of all the Called Shares held by it, the defaulting Shareholder shall be deemed to have irrevocably appointed any person, nominated for the purpose by the Board, to be its agent and attorney to execute all necessary transfers on its behalf and, against receipt by the Company of the purchase monies or any other consideration payable for the Called Shares, deliver such transfers to the Third-Party Purchaser (or as it may direct) and the Board shall (upon proper verification of payment of transfer tax, if applicable) immediately register the Third-Party Purchaser (or as it may direct) as the holder thereof and, after the Third-Party Purchaser (or its nominee) has been registered as the holder, the validity of such proceedings shall not be questioned by any such person.

The rights of redemption set out in the Articles of Association and the right of first refusal under Section 9.2 (Right of First Refusal) shall not arise on any Transfer of Shares to a Third-Party Purchaser (or as it may direct) pursuant to a Transfer in respect of which a Drag-Along Notice has been duly served. For the avoidance of doubt, a Trade Sale completed pursuant to the Drag-Along Option shall be subject to the liquidation preference provisions set out in Section 5.2 (Liquidation Preference).

    1. Tag-Along

Before a Shareholder (the Selling Shareholder) Transfers its Shares (or any part thereof) to any other Shareholder or to a third party (the Purchaser), each other Shareholder shall have the right to require the Purchaser to purchase a pro rata part of such other Shareholder’s Shares at the same price and on the same terms as the Shares of the Selling Shareholder. The Selling Shareholder shall not complete any such Transfer unless the tag-along right has been offered to all other Shareholders in accordance with this Section 9.5.

The Selling Shareholder shall notify the other Shareholders in writing of the identity of the Purchaser and all terms of the Share Transfer (the Selling Shareholder’s Notice) and the other Shareholders shall notify the Selling Shareholder in writing within fourteen (14) days of the receipt of the Selling Shareholder’s Notice whether they wish to exercise their tag-along right.

If the aggregate number of Shares proposed to be sold by the Selling Shareholder and the other Shareholders exercising their tag-along right hereunder would exceed the number of Shares which can be Transferred to the Purchaser, then each Shareholder exercising its tag-along right shall only be entitled to request that the Shares to be Transferred to the Purchaser are divided between the Selling Shareholder and the other Shareholders exercising their tag-along right on a pro rata basis based upon their ownership of all Shares.

If the Transfer of the Shares to the Purchaser has not been completed within ninety (90) days from the end of the fourteen (14) day period under Section 9.5.2 and the Selling Shareholder wishes to Transfer its Shares (or any part thereof) to the Purchaser, then the Selling Shareholder shall provide a new Selling Shareholder’s Notice and the other Shareholders will have a new fourteen (14) day period to inform the Selling Shareholder whether or not they wish to exercise their tag-along right.

If the Purchaser(s) refuse(s) to purchase Shares of the other Shareholders, as set forth above, simultaneously with purchase of the Shares of the Selling Shareholder(s), then the Selling Shareholder(s) shall not be entitled to Transfer their Shares to the Purchaser(s).

    1. Exit Transaction Costs

In connection with a Trade Sale, transaction costs incurred on behalf of the Company or all Shareholders collectively shall be borne by the Company. If such costs cannot ultimately be borne by the Company, for tax reasons or otherwise, they shall be deducted from the total consideration payable to the Shareholders before any distribution is made pursuant to Section 5.2 (Liquidation Preference).

Each Shareholder shall bear its own transaction costs incurred solely for its own benefit (including individual tax, regulatory or legal advice). Such costs shall not be deducted from amounts payable to other Shareholders.

  1. INFORMATION RIGHTS
    1. Financial Information

In addition to any and all information rights of the shareholders generally under the Companies Act, the Company shall provide to each Investor:

  1. within thirty (30) days from the end of each financial period, the annual unaudited financial statements for each financial period of the Company, including an unaudited balance sheet, an income statement as of the end of such financial period, an unaudited statement of operations and an unaudited statement of cash flows of the Company for such year, all prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and practices in Finland; and
  2. within thirty (30) days after the end of each quarterly period, the quarterly unaudited financial statements of the Company, including an unaudited balance sheet, an income statement as of the end of such quarter, an unaudited statement of operations and an unaudited statement of cash flows of the Company for such quarter, all prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and practices in Finland, subject to changes resulting from normal year-end audit adjustments.

The Company shall provide the Investors with audited records of any of the foregoing information once it becomes available and, as regards the information specified above in Section 10.1.1(a), in any event within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year of the Company.

    1. Inspection Rights

The Company shall, upon the written request of an Investor, allow such Investor and its professional advisors to visit and inspect during normal office hours at the expense of such Investor the Company’s properties and premises (excluding R&D premises), to examine its books of account and records, to take copies thereof and to discuss the Company’s affairs, finances and accounts with its officers, all at such reasonable times as may be requested by such Investor.

    1. KYC and Shareholder Information

Each Shareholder shall deliver to the Company any reasonable information, evidence or document to enable the Company to comply with all applicable laws and business practices, including, but not limited to information, evidence and documents relating to any “know your customer” (KYC) or anti-money laundering (AML) or similar identification procedures, when requested and within a reasonable time.

    1. Processing of Personal Data

The Parties acknowledge that for as long as the Investor is a party to this Agreement, the Company may disclose Personal Data to the Investor for the purposes of e.g. investment monitoring. The Parties agree that any processing of Personal Data shall be done in accordance with applicable law. The Parties further agree that it is the responsibility of the Company to ensure that it has the right to disclose Personal Data to the Investor for the given purposes.

  1. CONFIDENTIALITY

Each Party undertakes, and agrees with each other Party, except as authorised by this Agreement, to keep confidential and not to use, copy, disclose, divulge, or otherwise communicate or cause to be communicated, or to make available, any Confidential Information obtained from another Party (the Discloser) to any other persons other than its directors, officers and employees (together the Representatives) who have a need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement (including, without limitation, for the purposes of monitoring its investment in the Company). Each Party shall ensure that its Representatives are bound by appropriate confidentiality obligations and each Party guarantees the observance and proper performance by all of its Representatives of this Section 11.

The obligations and limitations set forth herein shall not apply to information which is:

  1. at any time in the public domain other than as a result of a breach of this Agreement;
  2. at any time rightfully received from a third party by the receiving Party without any obligation of confidentiality;
  3. rightfully known to the receiving Party without any limitation on use or disclosure prior to receipt of the same from the Discloser; or
  4. independently developed by the receiving Party or its personnel who have not had access to Confidential Information received from the Discloser.

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 11:

  1. each Shareholder is entitled to disclose Confidential Information to its attorneys, accountants, consultants, and other professionals, to the extent necessary for exercising its rights hereunder on the condition that the person to whom Confidential Information is disclosed is bound by confidentiality obligations substantially similar to those of this Section 11 or by a statutory confidentiality obligation;
  2. each Party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent Confidential Information is required to be disclosed by (i) applicable law, or (ii) an order of a court, an arbitral tribunal, or a regulatory authority, or (iii) a rule of a stock exchange to which such Party or its Affiliate is subject to; and
  3. each Investor is entitled to disclose Confidential Information to its Affiliates or for its fund reporting or investment management purposes and to prospective fund investors in connection with raising a new fund under the same management.

The Parties agree to keep in confidence the Confidential Information during the validity of this Agreement and three (3) years after the earlier of (i) the termination or expiration of this Agreement and (ii) the date on which such Party ceases to be a party to this Agreement.

Nothing in this Section 11 shall restrict the right of the Company to use Confidential Information in its regular Business operations.

  1. NON-COMPETITION AND NON-SOLICITATION

Each Working Shareholder undertakes, on behalf of itself and his/her/their/its Affiliates, during the validity of this Agreement and for a period of one (1) year after it has Transferred all its Shares, not to compete, directly or indirectly, with the Business provided that for the purposes of this non-competition undertaking the definition of Business shall not include any business that was not carried out or was not contemplated to be carried out by the Company or any companies belonging to the same group upon termination of this Agreement or when the Working Shareholder Transferred all its Shares. The above also includes the Working Shareholder, or his/her/their/its Affiliate acting, directly or indirectly, as an employee, financier, consultant, shareholder, member of the Board, advisor or in any other role in a company competing with the Business. Also, the preparation of any business competing with the Business by the Working Shareholder during the above non-competition period is prohibited.

During the validity of this Agreement and for a period of one (1) year after the Shareholder has Transferred all of its Shares, the Transferring Shareholder shall not directly or indirectly solicit (i) the employees or consultants of the Company or any of the companies belonging to the same group with the Company; or (ii) solicit or take away suppliers or customers of the Company or any of its Affiliates for his/her/their/its own benefit or for the benefit of any other party.

The Shareholders hereby expressly warrant that this Section 12 is fair and reasonable in all respects and that it does not unreasonably prohibit them from being employed or earning their living without breaching the prohibition on competition or the prohibition on solicitation. It is understood and acknowledged that investments not exceeding five per cent (5%) of any class of security traded on a stock exchange will not be considered to constitute breaches of the non-competition provisions under this Section 12.

The Board shall have the right, at the justified request made by a Shareholder in writing, to agree on exceptions (also in the adherence agreement(s)) to the above non-competition and non-solicitation undertakings on a case-by-case basis, subject to the written consent of (i) the member of the Board appointed by the holders of the Series Seed Shares or, if not appointed, (ii) the holders of the majority of the Series Seed Shares.

The Parties acknowledge that the Investors are engaged in investment activities. Nothing in this Section 12 shall prevent or prohibit the Investors from making or maintaining any investments or from appointing directors or representatives to the boards of directors of their investee companies.

In the event a Working Shareholder would be under an obligation to pay liquidated damages and/or compensation for damages for the same breach on the basis of this Agreement and his/her/their/its managing director agreement or employment or service contract, the liquidated damages and compensation for damages payable under his/her/their/its managing director agreement or employment or service contract shall be reduced by the amounts payable under this Agreement.

  1. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS

The Parties acknowledge and agree that the essential condition of this Agreement is that the Company shall have, without any separate compensation, all the rights, title and interest in and to all the Intellectual Property Rights arising out of the business of the Company and its Affiliates which are developed or generated prior to or after the execution of this Agreement based on the Working Shareholder’s employment, whether through a third-party company or otherwise, and in and to all the results of the Working Shareholder’s work.

Each Working Shareholder acknowledges and confirms that all output by the Working Shareholder and all Intellectual Property Rights pertaining thereto, together with all rights, title and interest therein, which have arisen or will later arise in conjunction with the Business and which have been or are created or developed by the Working Shareholder (or have been or are transferred to the Working Shareholder), either alone or jointly with others, during his/her/their employment or service relationship with the Company while performing duties based on his/her/their employment or service relationship or within six (6) months thereafter, are hereby and, in respect of future rights shall be automatically, assigned to, and be the exclusive property of, the Company or its Affiliates. Each Working Shareholder shall irrevocably and unconditionally waive all claims relating to any Intellectual Property Rights transferred under this Section 13 or the utilisation thereof against the Company and/or its Affiliates.

The Shareholders agree, without delay, at the request of the Company, to deliver to the Company all documents and other such information that relate to the confirmation of or transfer of the title to the said Intellectual Property Rights to the Company and/or its Affiliates, and also otherwise to act in such a manner that the Company or its Affiliates can make use of or register such Intellectual Property Rights or to maintain the registration in any country, authority or court.

The Company and its Affiliates shall have an exclusive right to utilise the said results and the Intellectual Property Rights transferred under this Section 13 commercially and industrially, transfer them to third parties, modify and further develop them without the separate consent of the respective Working Shareholder. In accordance with what has been set forth above, the Company and its Affiliates shall always have the right to use the results or the Intellectual Property Rights of the work performed also after the termination of the employment or service relationship of the Working Shareholder or termination of any other agreement regarding work for the Company and/or its Affiliates.

Should the Company or any of its Affiliates be deemed not to have received title to the said Intellectual Property Rights resulting from the work of the Working Shareholders in the Company and/or its Affiliates or for the Company and/or its Affiliates, the Company shall always, in accordance with what has been set forth above, have an exclusive, free of charge right of use thereof and, if it so wishes, the right to redeem such right. In such an event, the Company and its Affiliates shall also be entitled to transfer, modify and further develop the Intellectual Property Rights and to assign such Intellectual Property Rights or part thereof to third parties on the terms the Company deems best.

Each Working Shareholder agrees not to register or attempt to register during or after his/her/their/its employment or service any trademark, business name, domain name, email address or social media account, etc., that is confusingly similar, or refers to, any marks or symbols used by the Company or its Subsidiaries (including business name, auxiliary business name, trademark or domain name) or that is a derivative of any of the marks or symbols used by the Subsidiaries.

  1. TERM

This Agreement shall enter into force with respect to each of the Parties on the Effective Date and with respect to each new Shareholder upon signing a separate adherence agreement.

This Agreement shall remain in force as long as more than one Shareholder, directly or through a Holding Company, owns Shares. However, this Agreement shall terminate with respect to each Shareholder (save for the sections of this Agreement which are intended to survive any termination of this Agreement, including Sections 11 (Confidentiality), 12 (Non-competition and non-solicitation), 13 (Intellectual Property Rights), 15 (Material breach of Agreement) and 16 (Miscellaneous)), when such Shareholder has Transferred all its Shares in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and no longer holds any Shares. For the sake of clarity, any Transfer of Shares in breach of this Agreement shall not terminate this Agreement with respect to such Transferring Shareholder.

Termination of this Agreement (whether with respect to all Parties or a particular Party) shall not release any of the Parties, or such Party, as the case may be, from any liability under any obligation pursuant to this Agreement which at the time thereof has already fallen due for performance or any antecedent breach of this Agreement.

  1. MATERIAL BREACH OF AGREEMENT

Material Breach means (i) any breach of the non-competition or non-solicitation provisions under Section 12; (ii) any breach of the provisions of Section 9 (save for a breach of a procedural term provided the breach is rectified within the above thirty (30) day period and that no damage has been incurred to any other Party); or (iii) any other material breach of this Agreement which is not rectified, if capable of being rectified, within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice of default specifying details of the alleged breach.

In the event of a Material Breach by a Party (the Breaching Party), the Breaching Party shall pay to all non-breaching Shareholders pro rata to their then-current shareholdings liquidated damages in the amount of EUR [amount] per each Material Breach or, if the non-breaching Shareholders unanimously so agree, the amount of liquidated damages shall be paid to the Company. The liquidated damages do not limit the non-breaching Shareholders’ right to receive from the Breaching Party full compensation for all damages and losses exceeding the amount of the liquidated damages or for damages incurred prior to the remedy of the breach.

In addition to the liquidated damages under Section 15.2 above, the Company primarily and the non-breaching Shareholders secondarily shall be entitled, but not obliged, to redeem the Shares owned by the Breaching Party. The redemption price shall be the lower of (i) the original purchase and/or subscription price of such Shares paid by the respective Shareholder or (ii) the Fair Market Value of such Shares. If several Parties wish to exercise their right of redemption, the Shares shall be divided among the Parties wishing to redeem the Shares by the Board in proportion to the Shares owned by such Parties already. If the division of the Shares is uneven the residual Shares shall be divided among the Parties wishing to redeem the Shares by drawing lots.

  1. MISCELLANEOUS
    1. Further Assurances

Each Party shall execute such documents and take such actions as may be necessary, reasonably required or desirable to effectively carry out the provisions hereof and the transactions contemplated hereby.

The Shareholders shall not enter into any other shareholders’ agreement or be bound towards any Shareholder by way of any other commitment or agreement with respect to the Shares and/or the Company unless all the Shareholders are parties to such agreement (such as a separate minority shareholders’ agreement) or other commitment.

    1. Amendments

Subject to Section 6.2, any amendment to this Agreement shall be in writing and shall have no effect before signed by duly authorised representatives of all Parties save for adherence of a new Shareholder in accordance with Section 9.3.

    1. No Waiver

No waiver by any Party of any right or remedy under this Agreement shall be effective unless given in writing and executed by or on behalf of the duly authorised representative(s) of such Party. Any failure or delay by a Party in exercising any right or remedy will not constitute a waiver. No waiver of any term or condition of this Agreement or of any right or remedy arising in connection therewith shall constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of such provision or waiver by such Party of any breach of any other provision hereof.

    1. Notices

All notices and other communications given or made pursuant to this Agreement shall be in English, in writing and shall be deemed effectively given upon the earlier of actual receipt or:

  1. upon receipt, if delivered personally to the Party to be notified;
  2. once sent, if sent by email during normal business hours of the recipient, and if not sent during normal business hours, then on the recipient’s next business day;
  3. five (5) business days after having been sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or
  4. one (1) business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, freight prepaid, specifying next business day delivery, with written verification of receipt.

All communications shall be sent to the respective Parties at their address as set forth in Section 1 or as set forth in a separate adherence agreement, or to such address or email address as subsequently notified by the respective Party by a written notice and such notice shall be deemed given when received by the other Parties in accordance with Section 16.4.1.

    1. Entire Agreement

This Agreement and the documents referred to herein, together with all the Schedules hereto, constitute the entire agreement and understanding of the Parties with respect to the subject matter of this Agreement, and supersede any and all prior understandings and agreements, whether oral or written, between or among the Parties hereto with respect to the specific subject matter hereof.

The Parties agree that in the event of a conflict between this Agreement and the Articles of Association or this Agreement and the Companies Act (save for any statutory stipulations), this Agreement shall prevail.

    1. Severability

If any provision of this Agreement shall be found by any court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unenforceable, the Parties hereby waive such provision to the extent that it is found to be invalid or unenforceable. Such provision shall, to the maximum extent allowable by law, be modified by such court so that it becomes enforceable as close to the original provision as possible, and, as modified, shall be enforced as any other provision hereof, all the other provisions hereof continuing in full force and effect.

    1. Assignment

This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, shall constitute any rights or remedies to any third parties under this Agreement unless expressly stated otherwise.

Any attempt without such permission to assign, transfer, delegate or sublicense any rights, duties or obligations that arise under this Agreement shall be void. Subject to the foregoing, and except as otherwise provided herein, this Agreement, and the rights and obligations of the Parties hereunder, will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of their respective successors, assigns, heirs, executors, administrators and legal representatives.

    1. Agreement Copies

This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts and all of the counterparts taken together shall be deemed to constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Agreement by email or execution by means of electronic signatures shall be as effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart of this Agreement.

    1. Governing Law

This Agreement, including the arbitration clause, and any dispute, claim or controversy arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination or validity thereof, are governed by the laws of Finland without regard to its principles and rules on conflict of laws.

    1. Arbitration

Any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination or validity thereof, shall be finally settled by arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration Rules of the Finland Chamber of Commerce. The number of arbitrators shall be one (1). The seat of arbitration shall be Helsinki, Finland. The language of the arbitration shall be English. However, evidence may be submitted and witnesses may be heard in Finnish, to the extent the arbitral tribunal deems it appropriate.

Schedule 1 – Form of Share Transfer Agreement

PARTIES

  1. [Name and contact details of the Good / Bad Leaver] (the Seller); and
  2. [Name and contact details of the purchaser] (the Purchaser).

The Seller and the Purchaser are hereinafter referred to collectively as the Parties and each separately as a Party.

  1. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE

The Parties note that the Seller is regarded as a [Bad Leaver / Early Leaver / Good Leaver] pursuant to Section 8 (Purchase of Shares from Working Shareholders) of the shareholders' agreement dated [●] by and between the Parties and certain other parties (the Shareholders’ Agreement) and that this agreement (the Agreement) effects the purchase of the Seller's Shares in accordance with Sections 8.3.1 – 8.3.3 of the Shareholders' Agreement. Capitalised terms used but not defined in this Agreement have the same meaning as in the Shareholders' Agreement.

  1. SALE AND PURCHASE

The Seller hereby sells, and the Purchaser hereby purchases from the Seller, [●] issued and outstanding shares in [●] Oy (the Company), corresponding to the share numbers [●] to [●] (the Shares).

Full and unrestricted title without any encumbrances to the Shares shall pass from the Seller to the Purchaser upon the payment of the Purchase Price by the Purchaser to the Seller as detailed below.

  1. PURCHASE PRICE; PAYMENT OF THE PURCHASE PRICE; TRANSFER TAX

The purchase price for the Shares is EUR [●] (the Purchase Price). The payment term for the Purchase Price is fourteen (14) days from the signing of this Agreement.

Any transfer tax payable in relation to the sale and purchase of the Shares shall be paid by the Purchaser.

  1. WARRANTIES

The Seller represents and warrants to the Purchaser on the date of this Agreement as follows:

  1. the Seller has the full legal power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to consummate the sale of the Shares pursuant to this Agreement and this Agreement constitutes a binding obligation of the Seller enforceable against it in accordance with the terms of this Agreement;
  2. the execution of this Agreement and the consummation of the sale of the Shares pursuant to this Agreement does not and will not result in a breach of any judgement or order of any court, governmental or other body, any applicable law or regulation, or any agreement binding on the Seller; and
  3. the Seller owns the Shares, the Shares are freely transferable to the Purchaser and are free and clear of any and all pledges, mortgages, liens, options or other third party rights of any kind, and all transfer and other taxes levied on or in relation to previous transfers of the Shares, if any, have been duly paid.
  4. MISCELLANEOUS

Sections 11 (Confidentiality), 15 (Material Breach of Agreement) and 16 (Miscellaneous) of the Shareholders’ Agreement shall apply mutatis mutandis to this Agreement.

The Parties' contact details for the purposes of Section 16.4 (Notices) of the Shareholders' Agreement are as set out in Section 1 of the Shareholders' Agreement or as otherwise notified to the Company.

This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts and all counterparts taken together shall be deemed to constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Agreement by email or signing of this Agreement electronically shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart of this Agreement.
